deep.reconstruction:
The page holds no derivation. It is a draft of numbered 'theses' on optics. The struck-out heading reads roughly 'Thesen zur Optik'. These are the kind of short propositions a candidate defended at a Göttingen doctoral or habilitation disputation. The draft breaks off before any formula.

Thesis 1 (methodological). The common foundation of all laws of light propagation confirmed by experience is the system of partial differential equations of light propagation. A further explanation of these equations from (attractive/repulsive) central forces is not demanded by experience. This rejects reducing optics to a molecular ether model with central forces between particles, the approach of Cauchy, Poisson and Neumann. Riemann takes the field PDEs themselves as the primary physical law. This matches his known natural-philosophical stance, field action and contiguous action rather than action at a distance, seen in the 1858 paper on electrodynamics and in the 'Naturphilosophie' fragments.

Thesis 2 (setting up the equations). Let t be time and x1, x2, x3 rectangular coordinates. Let u1, u2, u3 be the components, parallel to the axes, at the point (x1,x2,x3) and time t, of the cause called light. This cause is determined in magnitude and direction. A struck phrase uses a word like 'Lichtstoß/Erschütterung', and the light is thought of as a deviation from the equilibrium (rest) position.

The sentence then reads 'so sind die Differentialgleichungen der Lichtfortpflanzung im leeren Raum…'. A pencil revision changes it to '…lassen sich … in die Form bringen'. The intended equations are never written.

My completion (not on the page, conjectural): the standard form in empty space would be the transverse vector wave equation
∂²u_i/∂t² = c² Δu_i,
with ∂u1/∂x1 + ∂u2/∂x2 + ∂u3/∂x3 = 0 (Fresnel transversality).

A struck, unfinished line near the bottom reads roughly '…bleibt in Folge der Störung (zum Abschluß)'. The tally marks at the bottom are unrelated counting.

results.what: Methodological thesis: the PDEs of light propagation are the empirically grounded foundation of optics; reducing them to central forces between ether particles is not required by experience.
results.modern_name: Field-theoretic (phenomenological) view of optics, as opposed to the molecular-force ether models of Cauchy/Neumann
results.usually_credited_to: Broadly the field viewpoint is associated with Faraday and Maxwell (1860s) and, in Germany, with Riemann's own natural philosophy and 1858 electrodynamics note

results.what: Setup of light as a vector displacement field u(x,t), a deviation from equilibrium, governed by PDEs in empty space (equations not written)
results.modern_name: Vector wave equation for the luminiferous ether / elastic-wave model of light
